artworks.title: The North Front of Old Somerset House in the Strand
artworks.medium: etching, aquatint, and mezzotint on laid paper
artworks.description: The image shows a grand architectural facade, likely from the 18th or 19th century, featuring a central building flanked by symmetrical wings. The roofline of the building has tall chimneys, against a cloudy sky. The artwork is rendered in detailed ink wash or sepia tones. In the foreground, there is a cobbled street with a horse-drawn carriage and pedestrians. There is a wrought iron fence running parallel to the building. The color palette is predominantly beige and brown.

artworks.title: Il Carnevale di Roma (Carnival in Rome)
artworks.creditLine: Purchased as the Gift of Vincent J. Buonanno
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a street scene during a festival or parade. The drawing depicts a busy street with a crowd of people engaged in various activities. Some are around a central figure on a raised platform, and flags and banners are visible. Some individuals are on horseback. Surrounding buildings are shown, adding depth to the scene.

artworks.title: The Inner Courtyard of Old Somerset House in the Strand
artworks.medium: etching, aquatint, and mezzotint on laid paper
artworks.description: The image shows a courtyard scene with a central viewpoint providing a wide angle of the architecture. The central building has a clock tower with a weather vane. The drawing has precise lines and shading detailing the stonework and windows. The color scheme is sepia tones, creating an antique feel. In the foreground, there are people engaged in various activities, including conversing and holding a dog. A horse-drawn coach is under the arches, with other figures moving around. Clouds in the sky add to the period ambiance.

artworks.title: Wooded Landscape with Figures outside a Cottage
artworks.medium: watercolor over graphite with scratching out on wove paper, laid down
artworks.description: The image shows a rural scene with a path curving towards the horizon. In the foreground, there's a tree on the right with vines on its trunk, and on the left, a tree frames a house where figures are gathered near the entrance. The background consists of misty, distant trees. The brushwork is a mix of detailed and soft strokes, and the color palette includes earth tones, blues, and yellows.

artworks.title: Bust of a Young Woman in Profile
artworks.creditLine: Purchased for the Virginia and Ira Jackson Collection
artworks.description: The image depicts a sketch of a profile view of an upper body. The subject's face is turned to the side, showing their facial features such as the nose, lips, and chin. The hair is styled with volume at the top and swept back. The clothing is suggested with simple lines indicating a draped garment. The background is shaded with a dark texture, with no visible jewelry or objects being held.

artworks.title: Plate Number 667. Ass; walking, saddle; a boy riding, Zoo
artworks.description: This is a series of photographs depicting a mule walking under saddle. The sequence shows the mule's motion from different angles: side and rear views. The first two rows display a side profile of the mule from a consistent angle, illustrating the steps as it walks forward. The photos capture various gait phases, with each frame showing incremental movement. The lower row contains a rear view, displaying the mule's leg movement, body, and tail. Each frame is numbered to show progress within the series. The black and white images suggest an archival or classic photographic style, reminiscent of early motion studies like those by Eadweard Muybridge.

artworks.title: Plate Number 668. Ass; ambling; irregular; saddle; a boy riding, Zoo
artworks.description: This is a series of sixteen monochromatic images of a donkey in motion. The upper two rows show a side profile view, while the lower two rows show a rear view. The images capture the sequential movements of the donkey walking. Each image seems to be part of a scientific study on gait analysis. The grid backdrop adds a sense of measurement and precision.

artworks.title: Plate Number 672. Ox; trotting
artworks.description: This is a photograph of a sequence showing the movement of an animal walking. The image includes sixteen individual black-and-white shots arranged in four rows, capturing the stages of the animal's gait. Each frame displays the animal in a slightly different position as it progresses through a walking cycle, providing a detailed study of its motion. The consistent backdrop and grid lines emphasize the changes in the animal's leg positions and body posture from one frame to the next.

artworks.title: Plate Number 671. Ox; walking
artworks.description: This is a photograph showing a cow walking. It is a sequential study capturing the motion of the cow as it walks. The image is divided into two rows, with the top two rows displaying side views of the cow across multiple frames, each showing a slightly different position in its walking cycle. The bottom two rows show rear views of the same motion sequence, again with each frame capturing a slightly different moment in time as the cow walks forward. The background grid provides a sense of scale and helps highlight the progression of movement over time. The image gives a sense of how the cow's legs and body move in a coordinated fashion as it walks.

artworks.title: Secret derobé à un ami (Secret Stolen from a Friend)
artworks.medium: etching on laid paper, inlaid in nineteenth-century paper mount
artworks.description: This drawing features a mythological figure seated on a barrel or drum, with a smaller scene framed inside. The central figure is depicted as a classical or mythological character, adorned with leaves and vines and holding a tray in one hand and a bottle or jug in the other. The figure's lower part forms an arch around another scene within a circular frame that shows an elegantly dressed person seated inside a richly decorated interior. The drawing has intricate line work characteristic of engraving, and its monochromatic palette emphasizes the detail in the figures and the textures of the drapery and barrel.

artworks.title: The Bodies of Saints Peter and Paul Hidden in the Catacombs
artworks.description: The image displays an abstract composition of swirling lines and textured shapes. In the lower part, there is a form resembling a human figure in repose, covered with drapery. The upper portion features dense and rugged patterns that suggest a forest canopy or trees. Small human figures are integrated into the natural setting.

artworks.title: Virgin and Child with the Prophet Daniel and Mary Magdalene
artworks.medium: pen and brown ink with brown wash, heightened with white gouache, over traces of black chalk, squared in black chalk, on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Ruth and Jacob Kainen Memorial Acquisition Fund
artworks.description: The image shows a drawing of four figures positioned under a large tree. In the foreground, a man standing to the left with a bushy beard, dressed in a robe and holding a staff. In front of him, two seated women with curly hair and drapery, one holding a child. The child is interacting with an object held by one of the women. A small dog is near the standing man's feet. The background features leafy branches and foliage, with a drapery behind the tree.

artworks.title: The Marriage of Alexander and Roxana
artworks.medium: etching with aquatint printed in brown on laid paper
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a scene featuring mythological elements. The artwork shows a group of winged cherubs, a seated figure, and other figures around an urn and draped fabric. The cherubs are engaged in different activities such as offering a crown, holding garlands, or playing together. The style is reminiscent of Raphael, known for classical compositions. The drawing has a monochromatic tone with sepia hues, giving it an antique feel, and detailed line work typical of the Renaissance period.

artworks.title: Theater Program for Sleeping Beauty, Silver Wedding, and Ahasvère
artworks.medium: color lithograph on wove paper [proof before letters]
artworks.creditLine: Purchased as the Gift of Jeff Atlas in memory of Liane and Martin Atlas
artworks.description: This is a painting of an interior scene in a restaurant or café featuring two customers reading newspapers. The setting includes red upholstered seating, a row of mirrors on the wall, and details such as a bottle and a glass on a table. The image conveys a sense of everyday life and leisure in a public dining space. The design style is reminiscent of Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec, with a focus on urban social settings and the use of simplified forms and strong outlines.

artworks.title: Plate Number 669. Ox; walking
artworks.description: This is a series of sixteen sequential frames showing a cow walking. Each frame captures a different stage in the cow's walking cycle, arranged in four rows with four frames in each row. The cow is depicted in profile view, and the background is a plain, grid-lined backdrop. The style of photography is similar to the work of Eadweard Muybridge, known for capturing animal locomotion through photography.

artworks.title: Plate Number 673. Sow; walking
artworks.description: This is a photograph of a series of frames capturing the motion of a pig. The image contains two rows, each showing multiple frames documenting the movement of a pig. In the top row, the pig is seen in profile, moving from right to left in front of a wire fence. The bottom row displays the pig approaching the camera, providing a frontal view of its motion.

artworks.title: Plate Number 676. Goat; walking
artworks.description: This is a photograph showing a goat in motion. It consists of multiple frames arranged in a grid format, depicting a goat walking from left to right. Each frame captures a moment in time, showing the sequential movement of the goat as it walks across a gridded backdrop. The goat's posture and limb positions vary in each shot, demonstrating the fluidity and mechanics of its gait. The images collectively encapsulate both a scientific and artistic representation of the subject's motion.

artworks.title: Plate Number 677. Goat; walking, in sulky
artworks.description: This is a photograph of a goat harnessed to a small cart in motion, presented as a grid of frames showing the progression of the goat pulling the cart. The background features a mesh grid. The top row shows a side view of the goat moving from left to right, while the bottom row shows a frontal view of the action.

artworks.title: Plate Number 679. Goat; galloping
artworks.description: This is a photograph of a goat in motion. The image shows a series of frames capturing the goat walking against a backdrop of a grid. There are four rows, each depicting a sequence of movement where the goat is slightly advanced in its walking stride, showing various stages of its gait. The background grid helps to illustrate the change in position from one frame to the next, emphasizing the fluidity and mechanics of the goat's walk. This sequential layout is characteristic of studies aimed at understanding motion through photography.

artworks.title: Plate Number 706. Dog; trotting; mastiff, Smith
artworks.description: This is a photograph showing twelve frames illustrating the movement of a dog walking. Each frame displays different stages of the dog's walking cycle, showcasing the positions of its legs, tail, and head from left to right. The background features a grid of horizontal and vertical lines. The dog, captured in a side profile, is wearing a collar.

artworks.title: Plate Number 713. Dog; turning around, etc.; setter, Kate
artworks.description: This is a photograph of a dog captured in motion in multiple frames. It shows a sequence of small photographs arranged in a grid, depicting the dog in various stages of movement. Each row captures the dog's progression against a lined background and in an outdoor setting with drapery present. The series shows the dog's limbs and body shifting positions, illustrating the dynamics of canine motion. The photography resembles the sequential studies conducted in the late 19th century, famously pioneered by Eadweard Muybridge, who captured animals and humans in motion.

artworks.title: Plate Number 714. Dog; aroused by a torpedo; mastiff, Smith
artworks.description: This is a photograph of a dog in twelve separate frames, each showing different moments of the dog's movements in a grid format. The frames display actions like walking, standing, and lying down against a grid pattern background. The series captures the fluidity of the dog's movements, showcasing its grace over time. It appears to be a study of motion, potentially for scientific or artistic purposes.

artworks.title: Plate Number 716. Cat; walking; change to galloping
